messages:
soren: Quick follow-up from the RFC — proposing a negotiated framing upgrade for streaming responses to address proxy chunking and client parsing fragility. need ops + infra + runtime opinions.
elaine: Can you sketch the new framing? is this changing wire format for websockets & http streaming?
soren: Short version: introduce `X-RW-FRAME: v2` header. v1 stays as chunked SSE/line-delimited events. v2 will be length-prefixed frames (4-byte big-endian length + payload) — smaller parser surface, deterministic boundaries, easier race handling. No change to payload schema.
tim: length-prefixed makes sense for performance. question: where do we translate? gateway sidecar vs runtime sidecar vs client lib?
elaine: Runtime can emit v2, but many customers use plain HTTP/ALB or old proxies that break on mid-stream flushes. We should offer a gateway-level translation that accepts v2 from runtime and emits v1 to legacy clients.
lucy: SRE concerns: translating at gateway adds CPU & mem pressure. need to estimate per-req copies and tail latencies. also, head-of-line blocking if gateway buffers full frames.
soren: Agreed. Proposed tradeoffs:
- Gateway translation (opt-in): minimal runtime changes, centralized control, easier telemetry. higher infra cost.
- Runtime dual-emit: runtime streams v2, but if `X-RW-FRAME: v1` present, it also emits v1 stream concurrently (two outputs) — lowest gateway cost, higher runtime complexity.
- Sidecar per-tenant: runs next to runtime, converts on host. middle-ground.
tim: We should support two negotiation modes: explicit header `X-RW-FRAME` and server-driven detection via `Accept`/`Upgrade`. Start with header to simplify.
soren: Rollout plan idea:
1) Add runtime support to emit v2 and a `Negotiation: can-v2` metric.
2) Deploy gateway translator behind a feature flag; default OFF.
3) Gradual opt-in: `X-RW-FRAME: v2` clients get v2 wire; others get v1.
4) Canary: 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% traffic by tenant id. monitor `stream.frame.errors`, `stream.parse-time`, `gateway.mem-alloc`.
5) After 3 months and stable metrics, flip default to v2 on new SDKs, keep gateway translator as fallback for 12 months.
elaine: Need a clear kill-switch and per-tenant safety gates. Also list of quick regressions to monitor (parse errors, client disconnects, increased 5xx).
lucy: For telemetry naming: `streaming.handshake.v2.accepted`, `streaming.frame.errors`, `streaming.gateway.buffered_bytes`. Add sample dashboards and an alert if `frame.errors` > 0.5% sustained over 5m.
tim: Implementation note: use zero-copy where possible. For nginx-ish frontends, we can detect header and proxy_pass to `v2-gw` upstream which does translation in C++; avoids Python copies.
soren: Example nginx route we discussed:
```
map $http_x_rw_frame $upstream {
  default         v1-backend;
  "v2"           v2-backend;
}
server {
  location /stream {
    proxy_pass http://$upstream;
    proxy_buffering off;
  }
}
```
tim: For the gateway translator itself, simple loop: read varint/4-bytes length, forward as SSE chunk `data: <payload>\n\n` and flush. reverse when client asks v2. Add per-stream quota to prevent OOM.
elaine: Edge case: multi-part responses (mixed event types) and function-calling frames — make sure we preserve event boundaries and metadata headers. will add tests.
soren: Backcompat policy text (short):
- v1 supported indefinitely for existing tenants.
- New tenant SDKs will default to v2 after 90d notice.
- Gateway translator kept for 12 months after v2 default, then reevaluate.
- Deprecation announcements + migration tooling (client libs, examples).
lucy: Ops runbook checklist:
- Canary rollout steps + rollback instructions.
- Dashboard links + alert thresholds.
- Memory/cpu baseline + expected delta.
- Contact list for oncall.

putting ownership: eng-runtime implements v2 emission + tests; eng-infra provides gateway translator + nginx routing; eng-sre owns canary monitoring & alerts.
elaine: +1 to owners. I'll write the test matrix (end-to-end with ALB, envoy, basic proxied clients).
_tim note: I can prototype a C++ streaming translator in ~3 days if we pair on interface.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: `gateway-translation-flag` -> deploy window 2026-04-02 01:00 UTC (canary 1%).
soren: Action items: elaIn test matrix, tim prototype translator, lucy dashboard & alerts, i'll draft the deprecation policy message & SDK notes. We'll sync Thu 11am. :thumbsup:
